# OPERAVA MailDesk — LLM Implementation Reference

## Authority
Current source code + applied migrations are authoritative. `docs/current-implementation.md` describes live behavior. `docs/architecture.md` describes target/planned architecture. Never present planned functionality as implemented.

## Stack
Static HTML/CSS/JavaScript; Supabase Auth; Cloudflare Worker; Supabase Postgres/RLS; Resend; Cloudflare Pages.

## Authentication
Supabase Auth is the only end-user authentication authority. Protected Worker calls use `Authorization: Bearer <Supabase access token>`. Do not add ADMIN_EMAIL/ADMIN_PASSWORD, fake sessions, query-string bypasses, or a parallel auth proxy.

## Browser configuration
Browser-safe only: Supabase URL, Supabase anon/publishable key, Worker URL.
Never expose: service-role key, Resend API key, Resend webhook secret.

## Worker routes currently implemented
- GET /health
- POST /webhooks/resend
- GET /me (authenticated)
- POST /ai/draft (authenticated Workers AI drafting; no mail/data mutation)
- GET /emails (authenticated)
- GET /emails/:id (authenticated)
- POST /emails (authenticated)
- PATCH /emails/:id (authenticated mailbox flags)

PATCH flags: is_read, is_starred, is_archived, is_deleted.

## AI drafting
POST /ai/draft uses the real `env.AI` Workers AI binding and server-side `AI_MODEL`. It validates input sizes and returns draft text only. It must never claim mail was sent or perform irreversible actions. AI provider/binding failures fail explicitly.

## Database
- 0001_maildesk.sql: emails, email_events, mailbox_status, RLS, Realtime publication.
- 0005_inbound_updates.sql: direction/from_address.
- 0006_mailbox_foundation.sql: mailbox flags and thread/folder/attachment metadata foundations.

Schema foundations do not imply live UI/API workflows.

## Resend
Worker sends outbound mail. Signed webhook ingestion verifies HMAC/timestamp and persists events idempotently. Current explicit status transitions: email.sent -> sent; email.bounced -> failed; email.complained -> failed.

## Request/error conventions
Worker emits x-request-id on newly hardened routes/responses. New API errors should use `{"error":{"code":"...","message":"...","requestId":"..."}}`. Preserve RLS as the authorization boundary.

## Planned, not live
- browser Realtime subscription
- production inbound ingestion route
- thread API/UI
- folder CRUD API/UI
- attachment Storage/upload/download
- full-text search
- drafts-specific API
- rich-text editor
- full delivery/open/click tracking
- comprehensive automated E2E suite

## Documentation requirement
When implementation changes, update `docs/current-implementation.md`, `docs/api.md`, relevant security/database/operations docs, README if user-facing behavior changes, and this file in the same branch.


## Production-only implementation contract
This is not a mock/demo repository. Never add fake users, fake messages, fake API success, simulated provider responses, placeholder production endpoints, or disconnected controls. If a production dependency is unavailable, fail explicitly.

## Design contract
Read and obey `docs/design-system.md`. Preserve the existing OPERAVA cream/off-white garden theme, purple-orange accents, Georgia display headings, sans-serif application typography, rounded surfaces, existing navigation/information architecture, responsive behavior, and repository brand assets. Do not introduce an unrelated UI framework/theme or incidental redesign.

## Cloudflare AI
Cloudflare Workers AI is the production AI runtime. `worker/wrangler.toml` binds `AI`; Worker code accesses it as `env.AI`. The model is selected server-side with `AI_MODEL`. Read `docs/cloudflare-ai-deployment.md` before implementing/deploying AI. AI routes must use real inference, require appropriate Supabase auth, validate input/output, preserve deterministic authorization, and never directly perform irreversible actions from untrusted model output.
